Solana is an important blockchain network in the crypto space, famously known for its low transaction costs, fast processing capabilities, and high transaction throughput. APIs or Application Programming Interfaces, are rules that let 2 different softwares to interact with each other.

APIs on Solana help developers integrate blockchain functionality into their applications without having to operate or maintain their own RPC infrastructure or validator. Different APIs focus on different needs and factors, so for users it’s best to choose one that fits their needs depending on the data and performance. Here are our top picks for the best Solana APIs of the month:

Alchemy is a holistic platform with a wide range of options available for developers. It has JSON-RPC nodes, DAS APIs, and gRPC streaming. The broader developer platform is helpful for developers and teams alike with monitoring capabilities and development tooling options.

It also has a developer-focused space, which makes it convenient for everyone who wants to manage different blockchain integrations within a broader development ecosystem. Alchemy proves to be a good option for startups and developers who are building with multi-chain applications.

Helius simplifies the process of interpreting and organizing large amounts of raw blockchain information that developers need to go through with its enhanced APIs. The DAS API lets applications retrieve information about digital assets like tokens and NFTs.

The platform also offers webhooks that are useful for applications to keep track of wallet activity. Helius’s broader infrastructure also offers Solana RPC access, historical transaction data, and real-time streaming through LaserStream.

QuickNode’s Solana API supports JSON-RPC API and provides low-latency, Yellowstone-compatible streaming on Mainnet and Devnet. It is built to scale dApps on the Solana blockchain.

Developers can submit transactions, interact with smart contracts, build apps, and read blockchain data. It is especially a great option for developers who are building multi-chain dApps, DeFi platforms, and other enterprise blockchain solutions.

Triton’s API has been designed to help developers build reliable and scalable apps on Solana. It gives them access to the Solana blockchain data with its high-performance RPC endpoints and real-time data streaming services. The infrastructure also supports standard Solana RPC requests, Yellowstone gRPC streaming, and WebSocket subscriptions.

Triton is one of Solana’s original validators and has provided RPC since 2021. Devnet and testnet are provided to developers with every subscription, and JSON-RPC methods are used for reading accounts and tokens.

Dune API is also useful for developers and helps them retrieve, investigate, and analyze Solana transactions, wallet activity, and on-chain events. It translates raw blockchain data into structured information.

The Execution API on Dune is great for complex historical analysis, aggregated metrics, and querying specific Solana programs. The platform also provides interactive dashboards, real-time data access and analytics for Web3 research.

Chainstack helps developers build, scale and deploy dApps without having to manage complex blockchain nodes. Developers can connect apps to Solana through RPC endpoints and receive real-time blockchain notifications and account updates.

Users can also connect apps with standard Solana JSON-RPC methods and provide developer-friendly integrations and have blockchain data access.

APIs on Solana help to make blockchain developments easier and more efficient. Developers can improve the scalability of their projects and access real-time blockchain data. They bridge the gap between blockchain infrastructure and real-world applications and allow developers to focus on making innovative product rather than spending extra time managing data processing.

#5127. XRP Exchange Outflows Hit 5 Billion as Price Rebounds

XRP has seen traders withdraw large amounts of tokens out of major crypto exchanges, especially Binance, over the last 30 days even as the broad market volatility persists.

Despite the intense selling pressure XRP has witnessed over the past few months, data from the crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant shows that XRP’s exchange outflow has reached 5 billion XRP over the last month.

While the massive 30-day exchange outflow of 5 billion XRP is a relief signal because it signals persistent demand for XRP even amid the intense volatility, further data shows that the outflow is relatively low compared to levels seen in October.

Although the 5 billion XRP outflow is significant and November has yet to wrap up, the data shows that it marks a decent decrease from October, when total exchange outflows for the month reached about 5.7 billion XRP.

Despite the 700,000 XRP decrease in the metric, the outflows registered in the last 30 days are still considered substantial and have drawn attention from market analysts as they signal strong investor conviction even as XRP suffered larger price losses this month compared with October.

Usually, increases in the exchange outflow of an asset suggest that investors are moving assets off exchanges into external wallets, most likely to hold them for longer periods.

#5126. Ripple’s $900 Million Revenue Target Raises Questions About XRP’s Stagnant Price

Ripple’s growing business operations and ambitious $900 million revenue target are drawing attention to the disconnect between the company’s commercial expansion and XRP’s price performance.

Despite increasing its presence in institutional payments, corporate treasury management, stablecoin services and digital asset custody, Ripple has yet to see comparable strength in its native cryptocurrency.

During a November 19 interview, Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse addressed the disconnect, attributing XRP’s relative weakness to broader cryptocurrency market conditions and shifting investor demand.

He explained that digital assets remain sensitive to changes in market sentiment, with competing investment opportunities potentially drawing capital away from cryptocurrencies.

The executive pointed to SpaceX’s anticipated public listing and Anthropic’s stock market debut as developments that may have attracted capital away from liquid cryptocurrency holdings. He noted that selling pressure across the crypto market coincided with these events, although he provided no figures confirming direct capital movements from XRP into either company.

Despite the market downturn, Garlinghouse described Ripple’s business performance as particularly strong.

“Ripple has had a phenomenal year despite the fact that the market around crypto has come way down,” he said.

The company has been expanding beyond cross-border payments, targeting institutional brokerage, stablecoins, custody and corporate treasury services. The boss believes blockchain technology can make financial transactions faster and cheaper, creating opportunities across insurance, payments and the tokenization of traditional assets.

However, Ripple’s commercial success does not automatically increase XRP’s value. The company is privately held, and owning its cryptocurrency does not give investors an ownership stake in its business or a direct claim to its revenue. The company also uses stablecoins and traditional payment infrastructure where appropriate, meaning not every service it provides necessarily requires XRP.

Integration of artificial intelligence into corporate treasury services is another factor contributing to Ripple’s expansion. During the interview, Garlinghouse explained that AI-powered tools can help businesses monitor liquidity across different markets, identify currency shortages, and prepare for upcoming financial obligations.

For instance, the technology can alert corporate treasury managers when available funds in a particular currency may be insufficient to cover upcoming payroll expenses.

Garlinghouse said these capabilities are already generating demand for the company’s treasury products.

“Adding intelligence and using AI agents to make your job easier is something we are doing today and it has driven a ton of demand around our corporate treasury solution,” he explained.

Meanwhile, Garlinghouse expects cryptocurrency performance to become increasingly divided as investors pay greater attention to the practical applications and adoption of individual digital assets. This could mean that projects with stronger real-world utility attract more interest than those relying primarily on market speculation.

He compared the current enthusiasm surrounding artificial intelligence with the early internet era, acknowledging that investor expectations can sometimes exceed technological progress.

“Some days that hype gets ahead of reality,” he said, arguing that expectations and actual results eventually reach equilibrium.

That said, Ripple’s expanding operations will need to generate stronger demand for XRP itself before the company’s commercial success can translate into sustained price appreciation. Whether increased institutional adoption and the growing use of its financial services will create that demand remains a key question for XRP holders.

XRP’s price setup has printed higher highs in crypto charts on a monthly basis. With traders trying to locate the local price bottom, speculative positions are winding down on Perpetual markets. These two conflicting signals present a setup that has been witnessed once in 2022.

Recently, Turkish analyst Celal Kucuker dived into the monthly chart from Bitstamp, which shows XRP near $1 with an ascending green trend-line and price projections indicating potential moves to $3.19 and $5.94. The seasoned analyst framed $5 as achievable in the longer-term.

The X post attracted 522 likes and 31k views with mixed replies questioning near-term catalysts. He called XRP’ monthly setup “one of the best-looking charts”, adding that XRP has maintained a rising trendline formation since 2014, positioning $3.19 as the initial target in the next bull run.

The sentiment is bitter & the market mood resembles that of November 2022, latest research from Bitrue’s Research Institute states. The analysts at Bitrue analyzed a multi-cycle market data bundle from 2022 to 2026, showcasing similar levels of ‘extreme fear’ around 20.

Back in 2022, FTX fiasco has ambushed the global crypto markets with an uncalled for liquidation event erasing billions of dollars a day for consecutive weeks. The downswings in market value are also similar.

$XRP keeps repeating the same pattern.A false bottom.A bull trap.A period of range-bound consolidation.And only then, the real bottom.Every previous rally has begun after this sequence, not during it.The chart is currently in that intermediate phase.The "launchpad" isn't… pic.twitter.com/OehoKC8hSX

Schmidt’s chart examines XRP’s weekly price from 2017 through 2026, highlighting nearly-identical patterns across several market cycles.

Two months from the FTX-infused crypto beatdown, XRP’s holders roughly gained 190% from the recorded XRP price on November 21, 2022. It took them 8 months to gain 115%, but the OG altcoin backtracked to 60% of yearly gains one year after the FTX collapse.

On the other hand, Bitrue Research Institute offers some encouragement in their Futures market data findings. Since 2017, XRP’s price has finished below $1 six times on a weekly basis, but restored that level each time.

As the total number of burn transactions approaches the 22,000 mark, Shiba Inu’s token-burning activity is nearing another significant milestone.

This is a testament to the continuing efforts by the SHIB community to reduce the cryptocurrency’s massive circulating supply by sending tokens to unreachable wallet addresses. The tokens are sent to these dead wallets and are then permanently out of circulation.

The milestone is another sign of the community’s ongoing interest in Shiba Inu’s tokenomics as investors look for developments that could create stronger demand across the ecosystem.

#5119. 1Password confirms data breach – Could users face phishing attacks?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

1Password confirmed a breach on the 25th of November after an attacker copied customer records through compromised backend systems.

The company said password vaults remained protected, while the stolen information raised the risk of convincing impersonation attempts. For those unaware, 1Password is a password manager that stores passwords, passkeys, and other sensitive information in encrypted digital vaults.

1Password began investigating on the 19th of November after an attacker compromised an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The attacker used that access to push malicious code into backend services and download records for some customers.

Those included names, email addresses, account identifiers, creation and sign-in times, and non-secret technical metadata. The attacker also copied public keys, authentication parameters, and tokens from certain invitation, provisioning, and account recovery links.

1Password said those tokens alone could not grant access; users also needed to complete sign-in or email verification. The attacker also copied private source code and accessed the company’s software deployment systems.

However, it stated that it never stored account passwords or Secret Keys required to decrypt vaults.

The company disabled the compromised account and rotated potentially exposed credentials. It reported no internal evidence of account takeovers through exposed provisioning tokens.

The reassurance about vaults left a separate question hanging: how had one employee account enabled such extensive access?

Akash Network founder Greg Osuri said his trust was “heavily diminished” and called for an option to keep vaults entirely local. Crypto and blockchain CTO Nicki Sanders focused on the intrusion, stating,

The part that worries me is how they got in.

Trading Strategy co-founder Mikko Ohtamaa favored open-source alternatives, arguing that transparency could make persistent attacks easier to detect.

Others were less categorical. X user Tom Lombardi called the incident,

The disagreement extended to passwords themselves. Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) urged users to change all passwords.

After 1Password said passwords remained unexposed, CZ acknowledged the clarification and suggested weak-password checks and changing login emails to protect against phishing.

Stolen account details could help scammers impersonate 1Password through convincing recovery messages. That risk already reaches beyond email.

Unit 42 research tracked fake IT-support voice calls targeting over 150 employees across at least ten companies. The activity ran between January and April 2026.

Binance’s official risk account previously documented WhatsApp impersonators using supposed P2P account problems to solicit login QR-code scans. Ledger’s campaign tracker documented fake support calls and physical letters directing recipients toward recovery-phrase theft.

#5117. Ukraine Legalizes Crypto After One-Day Delay

Home » Regulations » Ukraine Legalizes Crypto After One-Day Delay

Crypto-embracing Bill No. 10225-d gets the highest-priority treatment following a slight procedural delay.

Ukraine’s parliament has approved a bill to bring cryptocurrency trading, custody and taxation under a formal legal framework.

The measure, Bill No. 10225-d, passed after lawmakers postponed consideration a day earlier, a pause that had raised questions about its immediate path despite renewed support from the parliamentary finance committee for the revised text.

The Ukraine crypto bill is designed to legalize and regulate the domestic virtual-asset market rather than leave it in a largely undefined legal space.

Its scope includes tax treatment for crypto activity as well as rules for trading platforms and custodial services.

That approach would place businesses handling customer assets under a clearer licensing and compliance structure.

BREAKING: Ukraine officially passes law to LEGALIZE crypto, effective July 1, 2027. pic.twitter.com/6KxnNa7N2b

The framework comes into practice on July 1, 2027. It offers more certainty over how digital-asset transactions are treated by authorities, though implementation details will matter as much as the legislation itself.

Ukraine has maintained an active crypto sector despite the strains of war, with digital assets playing a visible role in fundraising and cross-border transfers.

Formalizing the market has therefore carried significance beyond ordinary financial regulation: it could help define how crypto businesses operate in an economy still managing exceptional pressures with the fifth year of war with Russia coming along.

The Ukraine crypto bill’s journey shows how quickly crypto policy can shift even when lawmakers broadly support regulation.

The November 24, 2026 postponement followed committee backing for a revised version, while the subsequent passage points to a resolution of at least some of those immediate obstacles.

Questions remain over the final tax mechanics, the timing of licensing requirements and which agencies will oversee different parts of the sector. Market participants will also watch for secondary rules that determine the practical burden on exchanges, brokers and wallet providers.

Ukraine’s crypto move matters because it adds another sizable European market pursuing rules for digital assets rather than relying on prohibition or legal ambiguity.

The Ukraine crypto legislation may give local firms a route toward greater legitimacy, but the ultimate test will be whether the resulting framework is workable enough to retain innovation while improving crypto oversight.

#5115. Fidelity Files for Chainlink ETF. What Does It Mean for LINK?

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Fidelity’s Chainlink ETF proposal would hold LINK directly and trade on Nasdaq if it clears the remaining steps. The proposed Fidelity Chainlink Fund, described in a November 25 registration statement, would use the ticker FLNK, although the filing is preliminary and no launch date or final annual fee has been provided.

The larger question is not whether Wall Street can package LINK. It already has. The question is whether Fidelity can attract fresh demand for the token rather than divide the existing market among another set of fund shares.

The proposed fund would hold LINK, not a basket of blockchain companies or derivatives intended to mimic LINK’s price. Its objective is to follow the token’s U.S. dollar performance, less expenses and liabilities. The prospectus identifies Anchorage Digital Bank, BitGo Bank & Trust and Coinbase Custody as custodians, with the trust intending to hold its LINK on Ethereum.

Fidelity also lays out how the price would be measured. Its proposed reference rate uses prices from eligible LINK spot markets, with a volume-weighted median methodology calculated every 15 seconds using rolling 60-minute market data. That is a mechanism for valuing the assets. It is not a guarantee that fund shares will trade at precisely the reported value when markets are thin or volatile.

Nor is this a yield product. The filing states plainly: “The Trust will not stake its LINK.” Shareholders would not receive staking rewards through the fund. They would be buying securities designed to reflect an underlying token’s price, not a wallet balance they can use in Chainlink services.

That distinction matters because the company’s use of Chainlink technology elsewhere is a separate story. NewsBTC has previously reported on Chainlink infrastructure used with Fidelity’s tokenized FILQ fund. An investment vehicle that owns LINK is not evidence of increased demand for Chainlink’s oracle services, and using the network’s technology does not automatically mean buying its token.

This is not the first attempt to make LINK available through conventional securities accounts. Grayscale’s Chainlink Trust ETF, trading as GLNK, had a share creation and redemption program in place from December 2025, according to its SEC disclosures. The Bitwise Chainlink ETF, CLNK, also appeared in a January 2026 Nasdaq information circular.

And fund shares are not the only conventional route. In November, NewsBTC covered Charles Schwab’s rollout of direct LINK trading to eligible crypto clients. These routes do different things, but they establish a useful baseline: access is no longer the same problem it was when crypto products were confined to specialist exchanges.

Fidelity’s possible advantage is distribution. Its name and brokerage relationships may reach customers who would not open a crypto wallet or buy LINK on a trading platform. That is a credible reason the filing matters. But branding, however recognizable, cannot tell investors how much money will arrive once trading begins.

There is also the price of access. The preliminary prospectus leaves the sponsor’s annual fee blank. Until that figure is settled, it is impossible to make an honest cost comparison with competing LINK products. For investors choosing between wrappers around the same token, fees, trading spreads and the gap between share prices and net asset value deserve more attention than a new ticker.

The mechanics are worth getting right. The proposed trust would issue and redeem large blocks of shares through authorized participants, using cash or LINK under procedures described in the filing. Everyday investors would generally trade the shares on an exchange instead of placing orders with the trust.

Those are two different markets. When one investor sells an existing fund share to another, the trade does not by itself require the trust to acquire more LINK. Sustained net creations can increase a fund’s underlying holdings. Redemptions can do the reverse. A rising share price, meanwhile, may reflect a higher LINK price rather than additional tokens entering custody.

That is why the announcement alone provides no evidence of fresh institutional inflows. The Form S-1 is a plan, not a subscription report. It does not tell us how much outside capital will be committed, what portion might come from rival products, or whether investor interest will survive a difficult crypto market.

There is a fair counterargument. Fidelity could appeal to a materially different pool of investors and grow total demand rather than simply redistribute it. The filing establishes a possible channel for that to happen. It does not establish the outcome.

First, the registration statement must become effective and the proposed Nasdaq listing must move forward. The final prospectus should also resolve the missing fee and other commercial details. Those are immediate milestones, not formalities to be assumed away.

If the product launches, the more revealing evidence will arrive afterward: the number of LINK held, changes in shares outstanding, sustained net creations or redemptions, trading liquidity and discounts or premiums to net asset value. Comparisons with existing LINK funds would help separate fresh demand from investors moving between products.

Until those figures exist, the sensible interpretation is narrow. Fidelity wants to sell investors exposure to Chainlink through a familiar brokerage format. Whether that changes the market for LINK is still an open question, and one that a filing cannot answer.

KuCoin will delist Monero (XMR) on Nov. 30, the exchange announced on Thursday. XMR dropped as low as $436 after the announcement and lost almost 15% within four hours, according to Kraken data on TradingView.

In the notice, KuCoin said that XMR would be delisted "in accordance with the Special Treatment Rules of KuCoin." The exchange closed XMR deposits on Thursday and will remove the XMR/USDT, XMR/USDC, XMR/ETH and XMR/BTC pairs at 08:00 UTC on Nov. 30.

KuCoin will also shut down XMR trading bots, Convert swaps and Earn products before the delisting. Users can withdraw XMR until Dec. 31, and KuCoin said that it could close withdrawals earlier if the Monero network stops producing blocks or processing transfers.

On Thursday, KuCoin's XMR/USDT pair had $73.8 million in 24-hour volume, according to CoinMarketCap. It was the largest Monero spot market and accounted for 47% of XMR spot trading. HTX's XMR/USDT pair was second with $29.5 million.

KuCoin did not mention its XMRUSDT perpetual contract in the notice. The contract had $33 million in 24-hour volume on Thursday, according to CoinMarketCap. Binance had the largest XMR perpetual market with $89.3 million.

PerpetualCow, who promotes the Wagyu trading platform on X, also responded to the delisting. "Over 50% of users sourced their XMR indirectly from KuCoin; it fuelled ALL instant swap exchanges," he wrote on Thursday. According to PerpetualCow, instant swap services "don't have their own liquidity" and "simply wrapped around KuCoin and sold/bought into their order books."

In the same post, he wrote that Wagyu had done more than $1.5 billion in volume in less than a year. He also shared a screenshot of Wagyu's XMR-USDC market together with the post, and it showed $63.5 million in 24-hour volume.

Earlier in November, the MEXC exchange also delisted XMR. The exchange removed XMR spot and perpetual markets on Nov. 13.

OKX delisted XMR in January 2024, and Binance removed the coin on Feb. 20, 2024. Binance said at the time that it would conduct a deeper review "when a coin or token no longer meets this standard, or the industry changes." XMR fell more than 15% after the Binance announcement.

Kraken stopped XMR trading for clients in the European Economic Area at the end of October 2024. In August 2025, Kraken announced an XMR delisting for Canadian clients "due to recent compliance requirements in Canada" and disabled trading for them on Sept. 2, 2025.

#5113. Switzerland’s First Spot Bitcoin ETF BBIT Begins Trading on SIX

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Switzerland’s First Spot Bitcoin ETF BBIT Begins Trading on SIX

BIT Asset Management’s regulated fund brings direct spot Bitcoin access to Swiss retail accounts.

BIT Asset Management’s Bitcoin Fund ETF (BBIT), Switzerland’s first spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund, began trading on the SIX Swiss Exchange on November 26, 2026. Structured as a regulated Swiss collective investment fund, the product gives retail investors direct Bitcoin exposure through standard Swiss bank or brokerage accounts without self-custody.

The passive fund tracks the SIX Bitcoin Reference Rate and holds physical Bitcoin offline in cold storage at regulated Swiss custodian AMINA Bank AG, ring-fenced from the manager’s and custodian’s own assets.

BIT Asset Management describes BBIT as Europe’s currently active spot Bitcoin ETF, though public offering is approved only in Switzerland.

BBIT is listed on SIX Swiss Exchange and trades in both U.S. dollars and Swiss francs, with a target annual management fee of 0.19%. The fund launched with an initial issue price of $10 per unit and an allocation of 350 BTC, valued at more than $20 million at launch.

Switzerland’s Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) approved BBIT’s fund contract on October 20, 2026, following an 18-month review.

FINMA granted an exemption from standard investment diversification requirements, allowing the fund to invest exclusively in Bitcoin based on the cryptocurrency’s established trading history and liquidity.

However, the fund is classified as an alternative investment fund with specific risks, reflecting Bitcoin’s volatility and potential for substantial capital losses.

Unlike most European crypto exchange-traded products, which are structured as debt instruments and expose investors to issuer credit risk, BBIT operates under Swiss collective investment scheme legislation. This means investors hold fund units backed by ring-fenced assets, legally separated from the fund management company’s own assets.

Pernet von Ballmoos AG (PvB) acts as the fund management company and issuer, while BIT Asset Management serves as the sponsor and investment manager. Flow Traders has been appointed as the market maker, supporting secondary-market liquidity.

The fund also provides daily disclosure of its Bitcoin holdings and supports in-kind subscriptions for eligible institutional participants.

While BBIT is Switzerland’s first retail spot Bitcoin ETF, a physically backed Bitcoin product—the Jacobi FT Wilshire Bitcoin ETF—previously debuted on Euronext Amsterdam in August 2023 before Euronext listed it as inactive in February 2026 and liquidation proceedings began later that month. Meanwhile, SIX has hosted physically backed crypto ETPs since 2019.

The listing arrives with Bitcoin price hovering near $60,500 after heavy November outflows across U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs.

BIT—formerly known as Matrixport—expanded its Swiss fund footprint after acquiring and rebranding its Swiss asset management arm (originally rooted in Crypto Finance Asset Management).

This approval is a major step for Switzerland, as it allows everyday investors to gain direct exposure to Bitcoin through a regulated Swiss investment fund. It also shows that regulators are becoming more open to Bitcoin as a mainstream investment asset.

#5112. Bitcoin’s Recovery Faces a New Warning After $2 Billion in ETF Outflows

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

The Bitcoin recovery above $60,000 is offering some relief after a brutal November sell-off, but the money flowing through US spot Bitcoin ETFs tells a less encouraging story. The funds recorded more than $2 billion in combined net outflows over four consecutive trading sessions ending November 24.

Bitcoin’s return to the psychologically important price level follows a difficult week in which the cryptocurrency traded as low as approximately $55,300.

The rebound is welcome. What is less clear is whether buyers have returned with enough capital to sustain it.

The scale of the recent withdrawals deserves more attention than the recovery itself.

According to Farside Investors, US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of $582.3 million on November 19, followed by another $669.2 million the next day. Withdrawals continued on Monday and Tuesday, bringing the combined total across those four trading sessions to approximately $2.05 billion.

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounted for roughly $1.77 billion in net outflows during that period.

Wednesday’s figures are still subject to final reporting confirmation, although available data points to further withdrawals.

These numbers do not mean that every institutional investor is abandoning Bitcoin. ETF shareholders include different types of investors, from financial advisers and asset managers to individual traders. Some may be reducing risk, while others could be unwinding positions that were never intended as long-term investments.

What the figures establish is that the ETF market has experienced persistent net redemptions, even after Bitcoin’s substantial decline.

That is not the response bulls would ideally want to see from buyers following a major correction.

Earlier this week, Bitcoin fell below $60,000 again after an initial recovery above $64,000 failed to hold.

Glassnode’s November 24 report, titled The Canary in the Coal Mine, documented the severity of Bitcoin’s latest decline. The cryptocurrency reached approximately $55,300 on November 21, falling beneath the lows established during the summer.

That matters because investors who bought during previous corrections may now be sitting on losses despite having entered the market at what appeared to be relatively attractive prices.

Glassnode’s historical data reveals another uncomfortable detail. Long-term holders recently accounted for more than 75% of Bitcoin’s realized losses before their share fell back toward 50%. Similar periods of selling at a loss appeared during previous bear markets, although that alone does not establish that Bitcoin has reached a bottom.

Their behavior becomes particularly important when Bitcoin starts recovering.

Some holders may use a rebound to reduce their exposure or exit positions closer to their original purchase price. Others may be willing to hold through further volatility. Which group dominates will influence how much buying is required to sustain the next move higher.

A price that previously attracted buyers can become an area of selling pressure when the market approaches it from below.

This is one reason why reclaiming $60,000 should not automatically be interpreted as confirmation that the correction has ended.

There is a credible argument against interpreting persistent ETF outflows as evidence that Bitcoin must fall further.

Markets can begin recovering before investor sentiment improves. In fact, waiting for every major indicator to turn positive can mean missing a substantial portion of a reversal.

Glassnode’s latest research offers some historical perspective. Bitcoin’s realized losses relative to capital inflows over the preceding year have reached their highest intensity since the FTX collapse in 2022. Previous episodes of heavy losses have occurred near major market bottoms, but severe selling alone is not enough to confirm that a recovery is underway.

Bitcoin also trades across a much broader market than US exchange-traded funds. Direct purchases, overseas exchanges and other investment vehicles can absorb selling even when American funds experience redemptions.

The distinction is between evidence that a market can recover and evidence that it has already established a sustainable recovery.

Bitcoin’s latest bounce demonstrates that buyers are willing to step in at lower prices. It does not yet establish whether those buyers can absorb additional selling at higher levels.

If Bitcoin begins to hold its gains despite persistent ETF withdrawals, that would itself be an encouraging development. It would suggest that demand elsewhere in the market is capable of offsetting some of the pressure coming from the funds.

For now, the price and ETF data leave that question open.

Thursday’s Thanksgiving holiday adds another complication to the recovery. US equity markets are closed, removing a regular trading session for American spot Bitcoin ETFs while cryptocurrency exchanges continue operating.

The absence of new ETF flow figures during the holiday should not be confused with an improvement in institutional demand.

With fewer traditional financial market participants active, Bitcoin’s immediate price movements may also provide an incomplete picture of how investors are responding to the recent sell-off.

Friday’s shortened US trading session and the subsequent return to normal market hours will provide more useful evidence.

For traders, the important signals are whether Bitcoin can retain its recent gains, whether ETF redemptions begin to ease and whether buying remains strong enough to absorb selling when normal market participation resumes.

The $60,000 level may dominate the headlines, but the more convincing recovery will be the one that can survive without depending entirely on temporary relief from selling pressure.

Solana is four days away from matching a record last seen in 2022. SOL has lost 25.7% in November so far (as of Nov. 26). That's likely to become the cryptocurrency's ninth losing month this year. If December also ends in the red, that would bring the total to 10, the highest number of losing months in a single year in SOL's history.

In terms of percentage losses, 2022 was overwhelmingly the worst year for Solana. SOL lost 94.15% in 2022. So far in 2026, it's down 43.09%.

SOL declined every month between January and July. August brought a 41.5% surge, followed by another 14.56% gain in September. Then, October and November erased all those gains.

As of Nov. 26, Bitcoin had fallen roughly 21% in November. That provides some context. In October, BTC dropped 7.32%, while SOL lost 19%. Solana was already underperforming Bitcoin before November's losses accelerated.

Meanwhile, another source of demand is faltering. U.S. spot Solana ETFs have recorded $164 million in net outflows over the 30 trading days leading up to Nov. 25.

On Nov. 6, investors withdrew about $24 million from these funds. By Nov. 25, when SOL was trading around $70, the funds recorded zero net inflows. Lower prices had not yet brought ETF investors back in significant numbers.

Solana's network activity actually grew during the summer rally. Quarterly trading volume on decentralized exchanges (DEXs) increased 23% from the previous quarter to $197 billion in Q3.

Of that, a record $7.1 billion came from tokenized equities. That's roughly 3.6% of the quarter's total volume.

Much of the third-quarter growth came from memecoins, according to Bitwise. On Nov. 26, the memecoin platform Pump accounted for $1.29 million of the $2.69 million in daily protocol revenue on Solana tracked by DefiLlama.

For SOL to recover and break even in November, it would need to rise about 34.6% by Nov. 30.

If November ends in the red, even a small decline in December would give Solana a record 10th losing month of the year.

December ended lower in five of the last six years shown on the chart. However, six data points aren't much to base a forecast on.

#5109. MetaMask Brings Stablecoin Payments to Three Asian Markets With New Card Launch

Home » Blitz news » MetaMask Brings Stablecoin Payments to Three Asian Markets With New Card Launch

MetaMask expands its payment card to Japan, Thailand, and Vietnam for Mastercard transactions.

Cryptocurrency wallet provider MetaMask launched its payment card in Japan, Thailand and Vietnam on November 25, allowing users to spend its dollar-pegged mUSD stablecoin at merchants that accept Mastercard.

The move gives users in the three markets another way to use stablecoins for everyday purchases. Rather than transferring funds to a centralized cryptocurrency exchange before spending them, users can make payments directly through a card linked to their MetaMask wallet.

MetaMask Card uses mUSD, a US dollar-pegged stablecoin, to make payments at merchants that accept Mastercard. Users can pay online with their virtual card or in stores through Apple Pay and Google Pay. At checkout, the required amount of mUSD is converted into the local currency, such as Japanese yen.

In Japan, the card is available only as a virtual version and carries no annual fee. ATM cash withdrawals are not supported. Users can spend up to $10,000 per transaction and $15,000 per day.

Payments made with an mUSD balance at domestic merchants carry no transaction fee, while purchases at merchants outside the user’s country of residence incur a 1% fee.

To apply, users must access the Money tab in the MetaMask mobile app, register an email address and phone number, complete identity verification (KYC), and provide proof of residence.

However, the card does not support direct payments with every cryptocurrency held in MetaMask. Users must first convert assets such as USDC into mUSD before adding funds to their MetaMask Money account.

The Japanese cards are issued by New Zealand-based financial services provider Immersve Limited. MetaMask says its Money account retains a self-custodial structure, allowing users to maintain control of their private keys.

The expansion comes as stablecoin activity continues to grow across Southeast Asia, where digital assets are increasingly used for cross-border payments and transfers.

Chainalysis’s 2026 regional research shows that Thailand and Vietnam, alongside the Philippines, accounted for 14.4% of global small-value peer-to-peer transfers. The report also found that cross-border stablecoin activity exceeded domestic volumes in both countries, reaching $10.4 billion in Thailand and $6.9 billion in Vietnam.

Japan offers a different opportunity. Its developing regulatory framework and growing interest in stablecoins provide another market for MetaMask to test whether crypto wallets can become practical payment tools.

MetaMask first tested its payment card in the UK and Europe in August 2024 before launching it to US customers in February 2026. The service has since expanded to the European Economic Area, Canada, and parts of Central and South America.

#5108. Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Faces a 9% Jump at the Worst Possible Time for Miners

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Bitcoin mining difficulty is on course to increase by approximately 9% at the next network adjustment, expected on November 27. The increase would reverse much of the relief miners received less than two weeks ago, leaving operators facing tougher competition for block rewards while Bitcoin trades well below its previous highs.

Current network estimates put mining difficulty at 134.82 trillion, following a 9.13% reduction on November 14. If the projected increase holds, difficulty will climb back toward 147 trillion.

For miners struggling to keep their machines profitable, the timing is hardly ideal. The electricity bill remains largely unchanged, but the same hardware could soon generate less Bitcoin.

Bitcoin adjusts its mining difficulty every 2,016 blocks to maintain an average block production time of approximately ten minutes.

When blocks are produced too quickly, the network makes the mathematical conditions for discovering new blocks more demanding. When production slows, difficulty moves in the opposite direction.

The previous 9.13% reduction in Bitcoin mining difficulty gave active miners some breathing room. Operators could expect to earn more Bitcoin from the same amount of computing power, provided other conditions remained comparable.

The upcoming adjustment, expected at block 977,760, reflects a faster pace of block production during the current difficulty period.

A 9% increase in difficulty does not translate into an identical percentage reduction in mining revenue. Under otherwise unchanged conditions, expected Bitcoin production per unit of computing power would decline by approximately 8.3%.

Consider an operator whose machines currently generate 1 BTC over a given period. Following a 9% difficulty increase, the same machines would be expected to produce approximately 0.917 BTC over an equivalent period.

Nothing about the hardware needs to change for that reduction to occur. The network has simply raised the amount of work required to compete for its rewards.

Mining difficulty only tells part of the story.

A more useful measure of the industry’s financial condition is hashprice, which tracks the expected revenue generated by a given amount of computing power over a day.

Hashprice incorporates Bitcoin’s market value, network difficulty and transaction fee revenue. It provides a clearer indication of whether a miner’s hardware is generating enough income to justify keeping it switched on.

Recent network data from mining industry trackers puts daily hashprice at around $28 per petahash of computing power.

At that level, the economics can become uncomfortable surprisingly quickly.

Consider a hypothetical mining fleet with an energy efficiency of 20 joules per terahash and an electricity rate of $0.05 per kilowatt-hour.

Operating one petahash of computing power continuously would cost approximately $24 per day in electricity alone. Against $28 in gross daily mining revenue, that leaves just $4 before hosting, maintenance, cooling, financing and other expenses.

If difficulty rises by 9% while Bitcoin’s price and average fees per block remain unchanged, that daily revenue would fall to approximately $25.69. The remaining electricity-adjusted margin would shrink to less than $2.

The network adjustment is the same for everyone. Its financial consequences are not.

An operator with newer machines and inexpensive power may comfortably absorb the change. Another running older equipment could find that switching off part of its fleet makes more financial sense than continuing to mine.

The industry’s response to difficult mining economics extends beyond upgrading machines or negotiating cheaper electricity.

Some established Bitcoin mining businesses are redirecting infrastructure toward artificial intelligence and high-performance computing.

Access to substantial electricity capacity, established data centers and existing infrastructure gives certain operators alternatives that smaller mining businesses may not have.

This does not mean Bitcoin mining is disappearing. The projected difficulty increase itself suggests that blocks are being produced faster than the protocol’s target rate during the current adjustment period.

But the growing divergence between mining operators deserves attention.

A Bitcoin mining facility with access to inexpensive energy and efficient equipment operates under a very different set of economic conditions from a business relying on expensive financing and aging machines.

Rising difficulty does not necessarily make the entire industry unprofitable. It makes the difference between efficient and inefficient operators harder to ignore.

The prospect of shrinking margins raises an obvious question for Bitcoin investors: will miners need to sell more BTC to finance their operations?

There is a plausible case for additional selling from businesses facing substantial operating expenses or debt repayments. Mining companies cannot generally settle their electricity bills with anticipated future Bitcoin rewards.

However, network difficulty alone provides no evidence that miners have increased their Bitcoin sales.

Some operators hold substantial treasury reserves. Others sell their production regularly, regardless of market conditions. Businesses can also reduce operating expenses, shut down inefficient equipment or obtain financing instead of liquidating additional holdings.

Actual miner balance data, exchange transfers and company treasury disclosures will provide more useful evidence than the difficulty adjustment itself.

The immediate development to watch is whether the estimated increase materializes at the next adjustment block. After that, hashprice and changes in network computing power will help reveal how operators are responding.

Bitcoin’s protocol is doing exactly what it was designed to do. It adjusts the competition for block rewards without considering whether individual mining businesses can afford to remain competitive.

The machines that become uneconomical have always been the operators’ problem, not the network’s.

#5102. XRP Bulls and Bears to Get 3x ETFs Soon

Two proposed U.S. exchange-traded funds would give investors a way to bet on XRP in either direction, with one targeting three times XRP's daily return and the other targeting three times its inverse.

If XRP gains 5% in a single day, the bullish ETF would target a 15% gain, excluding fees and expenses.

If XRP loses 5% in a single day, the bearish ETF would target a 15% gain.

However, investors betting on the wrong direction could lose approximately 15% of their investment in a single day.

The next update is scheduled for Nov. 30. Following a recent amendment submitted to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the registration statements for these ETFs are now scheduled to become effective on Monday.

The issuer has repeatedly delayed the effective date. It remains to be seen whether the funds will start trading anytime soon.

The filing covers a total of eight ETFs, including bullish and bearish funds for Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), Solana (SOL) and XRP.

Even if XRP's price remains unchanged over multiple trading days, both ETFs could record negative returns.

Since the ETFs rebalance daily, it's important to remember that when the price changes direction, the next day's percentage return is calculated based on the investment's value after the previous trading session.

Let's say XRP rises from $2 to $2.20 on Monday and then drops back to $2 on Tuesday. If you hold XRP over these two days, you'll break even.

However, if you invest $100 in the bullish ETF, your position would close Tuesday at approximately $94.55, assuming the fund achieves its daily target and excluding fees and expenses.

If XRP increases by 10% from $2 to $2.20 on Monday, the bullish ETF would target a 30% gain. Your initial $100 investment would now be worth $130.

For XRP to return to $2 on Tuesday, it would need to fall by approximately 9.09%.

The bullish ETF would therefore target a loss of roughly 27.27% on Tuesday. But that loss would be calculated against your $130 position, leaving you with approximately $94.55.

Of course, the bearish ETF wouldn't fare any better.

#5100. OpenAI’s Codex helps amateur astronomer uncover two possible planets NASA’s data had missed

A SETI Institute astronomer independently recovered both signals after an OpenAI engineer used AI-generated software to search observations of 100,000 stars.

An AI-assisted search of NASA's archived telescope data has uncovered two possible planets, with preliminary checks by a professional astronomer recovering both signals.

In a Nov. 24 report, OpenAI detailed how two amateur astronomers used its Codex and Astra tools to search observations of millions of stars for previously overlooked planetary candidates.

Kevin Bond, an OpenAI engineer, used Codex to develop software that detects recurring declines in stellar brightness, a potential indication of a planet passing in front of its host star.

Bond combined existing detection methods into a program that deployed two AI agents. One identified promising signals, while the other subjected those findings to further examination.

Running the software against archived observations of approximately 100,000 stars from NASA's Kepler Space Telescope produced more than 200 signals, including 10 associated with previously confirmed planets.

Vishal Gajjar, an astronomer at the SETI Institute, independently recovered two of Bond's findings.

The first involved a relatively cool star, KIC 5689121, whose brightness declined every 13.8 days. OpenAI said the signal was consistent with a potential planet approximately 2.4 times Earth's diameter. The second, KIC 6691030, exhibited recurring dips every 4.8 days, suggesting a potential planet smaller than Neptune.

OpenAI says SETI Institute astronomer Vishal Gajjar recovered both dips in the same Kepler data Kevin Bond searched.

Each repeat interval gives astronomers a pattern to test in follow-up observations.

The traces illustrate timing with schematic dip shapes and depths. The causes of both dips remain unresolved.

Both traces use a common 28.5-day window from an arbitrary starting point. Their dips are spaced at OpenAI’s reported approximate intervals of 13.8 and 4.8 days. Positions are rounded to the nearest SVG coordinate.

The traces illustrate timing with schematic dip shapes and depths. The causes of both dips remain unresolved.

Please enable JavaScript to verify and send this form.

“Our initial checks are encouraging, and follow-up observations will tell us more.”

While Bond focused on Kepler's archived observations, another amateur astronomer, Ethan Byrd, used OpenAI's Astra to examine telescope data covering approximately 19 million stars.

Byrd developed two searches, including one targeting planetary candidates within habitable zones, where atmospheric conditions could allow liquid water to exist on a planet's surface.

His initial search identified 49 candidates. Byrd has submitted one to researchers working on NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) mission, and two others are awaiting submission.

Astronomers have used artificial intelligence to identify planets for years. In 2017, NASA announced the discovery of Kepler-90i using a neural network trained to recognize planetary signals in telescope observations.

General-purpose AI tools now let amateur astronomers develop their own detection software and search vast archives for signals earlier searches may have missed.

However, recurring declines in stellar brightness can also result from eclipsing stars or fluctuations in telescope instruments.

Astronomers could investigate Bond's candidates by observing their host stars at the predicted transit intervals and measuring whether gravitational forces from potential orbiting planets cause detectable stellar movement.

Establishing whether either signal represents an undiscovered planet could take months or years, OpenAI said.

#5098. Bitcoin Miners Go 98 Minutes Without Finding a Single Block

Bitcoin miners experienced their longest dry spell since July on Nov. 26. According to Galaxy's Alex Thorn, it took Bitcoin miners 98 minutes and 19 seconds to find the next block.

That's the third time in 2026 that miners have gone this long without finding a block. The wait ended at 18:28 UTC on Thursday.

For anyone trying to get Bitcoin transactions confirmed shortly after the previous block, the gap meant waiting more than an hour and a half.

Even if you paid a very high transaction fee, you would still have to wait until a miner found the next block before your transaction could receive its first confirmation.

Thursday's gap was the 69th longest since 2011, according to Galaxy Research. It was just three minutes shy of the threshold for the top 50.

And this year's other long gap lasted nearly two hours. On July 6, miners took 112 minutes and 26 seconds to find the next block (number 956,953). That was the 19th longest gap on record, according to Galaxy.

Bitcoin automatically adjusts mining difficulty every 2,016 blocks to keep the average block interval at around 10 minutes.

However,  blocks sometimes are found seconds apart. Other times, it takes well over an hour for the next block to be found.

At any given mining difficulty, the chance that a single attempt to find a block will succeed is incredibly small.

If miners have spent 90 minutes trying to find the next block, the chance of succeeding on the next attempt is the same as it was on the first attempt.

So the expected time until the next block is found is still 10 minutes, even if it's already been 90 minutes since the last block was found. That's assuming the network's total computing power and mining difficulty remain unchanged.

Assuming an average block interval of 10 minutes, Thorn said you could expect a gap of at least 98 minutes and 19 seconds about once every 18,600 block intervals.

That means such a gap should occur roughly once every four months, based on an average of about 144 blocks per day.

Galaxy examined 877,290 block intervals going back to Jan. 1, 2011.

Researchers identified 1,948 intervals where at least an hour had passed between the timestamps of successive blocks.

However, Galaxy flagged 97 of those intervals because an adjacent block had a timestamp that was off by at least 10 minutes. This raised questions about the actual length of those gaps.

The longest recorded interval is particularly interesting.

On Nov. 30, 2011, block 155,290 seemingly marked the end of a 144-minute-and-50-second gap.

However, the miner who found the next block had set its timestamp back by 65 minutes.

After excluding apparent timestamp errors, the longest gap was 141 minutes and one second, recorded on Oct. 13, 2011.

#5097. Zcash Whale Wakes Up After 9 Years, Moves $11.39 Million To Kraken

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

The coins date back to 2017, when Ethereum was still a relatively young network, decentralized finance barely existed and Zcash was attempting to establish itself as a more private alternative to Bitcoin.

Almost a decade later, the wallet is active again. And its owner’s reported acquisition price makes the transaction particularly interesting.

According to Lookonchain, the whale originally acquired 23,412 ZEC at an average price of approximately $215, representing an investment of just over $5 million.

The latest transactions account for roughly two-thirds of that original position, with at least 7,750 ZEC transferred to a Kraken deposit address.

At the reported transfer valuation of approximately $723 per ZEC, those 15,750 coins are worth around $8 million more than their estimated acquisition cost. That would represent a return of approximately 236% if the investor sold them at that price.

What makes this wallet fascinating, however, is what happened between those two valuations.

Zcash spent much of 2024 and early 2025 trading around $16 to $20 before staging a remarkable comeback. At $20 per coin, the whale’s original investment would have been worth less than $470,000, a paper loss of more than 90%, assuming the position remained intact.

Holding an asset through a temporary market correction is one thing. Holding it through years of declining relevance, while newer cryptocurrencies attract developers, investors and attention, is something else entirely.

Whatever the owner’s reasons for keeping the coins untouched, the decision has aged considerably better than it appeared to during Zcash’s quieter years.

It also explains why the available information tells only part of the story.

Lookonchain can identify an apparent exchange deposit and estimate its value. Establishing who controls the wallet, whether ownership changed privately during those nine years or what the investor intends to do next is considerably harder.

Even the reported acquisition price is an estimate rather than a verified record of the owner’s personal trading history.

That is an important limitation of on-chain analysis, particularly when dealing with a network explicitly designed to give users greater control over their financial visibility.

The renewed enthusiasm surrounding Zcash has attracted a different kind of investor from the one buying ZEC in 2017.

NewsBTC previously reported that Winklevoss Capital backed the launch of a dedicated Zcash treasury strategy, illustrating how exposure to the cryptocurrency has begun extending beyond traditional crypto wallets.

But the revival of an old cryptocurrency also comes with an interesting complication: investors who have spent years underwater finally have an opportunity to recover their capital or take profits.

That does not necessarily make the Kraken deposit bearish. A transfer to an exchange is not proof of a completed sale, and one wallet cannot establish a broader trend among Zcash holders.

Still, the transaction is worth watching. If more early investors start moving dormant coins onto exchanges, Zcash’s new buyers may find themselves absorbing supply from an entirely different generation of holders.

Nine years ago, someone reportedly committed more than $5 million to the idea of private digital money. Today, the blockchain offers a glimpse of what that investment has become.

Whether the owner has finished holding Zcash is a question the blockchain alone cannot yet answer.

#5096. Walmart’s Black Friday rollout reveals how AI agents could spend money without controlling your wallet

Spending limits, restricted payment access and single-use authorization tokens underpin the retailer’s approach to autonomous commerce.

Walmart is allowing shoppers to purchase Black Friday deals through Meta’s AI assistant Muse without sharing their saved card details.

The retailer announced the integration on Nov. 24, expanding its Agent Gateway to allow customers to discover products, build shopping carts, and complete purchases through conversations with Meta’s AI assistant.

Shoppers can ask Muse to find television deals, identify discounted products available for delivery or recommend items based on their preferences. Walmart handles product discovery and checkout through its Gateway, which connects external AI assistants to the retailer’s shopping infrastructure.

To make purchases, shoppers must link their Walmart accounts through a sign-in process that redirects them to the retailer before returning them to Muse.

When adding an item to their cart for the first time, shoppers establish an Agent Profile within their Walmart account and set a spending limit for the assistant.

The profile allows customers to distinguish AI-assisted purchases from other orders in their purchase history. They can also revoke the assistant’s purchasing authority by deleting the profile.

Walmart retains control of payment processing. Under its Agentic Access Terms, only shoppers can designate which saved payment method an AI assistant can use. External agents cannot add cards, change payment preferences or access raw card details, including full card numbers.

Instead, each transaction requires a short-lived authorization token tied to the merchant, shopping cart, purchase amount and session. The token expires upon use, requiring fresh authorization for subsequent transactions.

Walmart matches requests from Muse. The shopper manages spending and payment permissions in their Walmart account.

Shoppers check out inside Muse with a saved Walmart card. Walmart says outside agents receive no raw saved card details.

Walmart’s announcement leaves the exact Muse approval prompts and eligible locations and devices unspecified. The diagram depicts responsibilities and the shopping request.

The illustration shows the shopping request and the shopper’s account controls described by Walmart in the November Muse walkthrough and the payment provisions in its Gateway terms.

Walmart’s announcement leaves the exact Muse approval prompts and eligible locations and devices unspecified. The diagram depicts responsibilities and the shopping request.

The integration builds on Walmart’s Agent Profiles, introduced in October as part of its efforts to give customers greater control over purchases made through AI assistants.

By default, shoppers must approve purchases initiated by an agent. However, they can authorize assistants to complete transactions independently within a predetermined spending limit.

Walmart can still request additional confirmation even when a purchase falls within that limit. Its terms also allow the retailer to intervene when transactions exceed or conflict with a customer’s purchasing preferences.

The arrangement creates a framework for AI assistants to move beyond product recommendations and execute purchases on behalf of consumers without directly controlling their payment credentials.

However, Walmart’s launch announcement did not specify when shoppers using Muse would encounter additional approval requests after granting an assistant purchasing authority.

The retailer plans to extend its Gateway to more applications and AI assistants, potentially expanding the number of platforms through which customers can authorize purchases.

Walmart’s existing return policy applies to purchases completed through Muse, although the company has yet to specify which locations and devices are eligible for the rollout.

#5093. SWIFT Weighs XRP & ALGO Benefits vs. Quantum Threats

Home » Ripple (XRP) » SWIFT Weighs XRP & ALGO Benefits vs. Quantum Threats

PQC algorithms deliver the same core functions like regular cryptography, but absorb the quantum-computing hazards.

SWIFT, the largest European financial conglomerate, has just released their latest perspective on quantum computing threats, a topic the crypto community, including the XRP Army, has eagerly debated over the past few months.

The financial community is uniting towards building the post-quantum cryptography (PQC) service, which would replace the algorithms prone to breaking by quantum computing. This aligns with the roadmap of several DLT-based altcoins, including Ripple (XRP) & Algorand (ALGO).

Both of these Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) based chains are preparing for signatures that erases those threats, potentially fully implementing it by 2028. “Today’s cryptography is deeply embedded across systems, applications & processes”, – the paper states, carving out a transitional path.

Transitioning to new standards requires SWIFT compliant organisations to understand where they are exposed and manage change in a controlled, resilient way. Blockchain adoption comes as a no-brainer: SWIFT’s new ledger acts as a plug between multiple popular chains, including Ripple’s XRP.

Q-Day is coming. Are we ready?Quantum computing could reshape the foundations of financial security as we know them.Preparing for that future starts now, and it will take the financial community working together.In the latest article in our Perspectives series, Michael… pic.twitter.com/kjLteDKFeM

SWIFT’s statement urges companies not to wait for complete inventory of cryptographic assets, but rather prioritise their most critical and exposed systems, beginning the PQC transition. That’s where Algorand (ALGO) & Ripple’s XRP Ledger stands out from the regular crypto crowd. Algorand’s is leading the pack.

The chain’s workable quantum-proof mechanics are being gradually implemented from 2022, targeting broad quantum resilience by the last quarter of 2027. This includes more account features, multisig & solid research into a post-quantum VRF and consensus messaging. First Falcon-protected transfers hit the mainnet in 2025.

It already protects historical state and offers native quantum-resistant accounts that people can use today. On XRP’s part, the Ledger sports a well-documented, institution-oriented plan with a practical migration path (keeping the same address, dropping the old key) with a mid 2028 goal. However, that’s still pre-development aspirations.

🚨 Many people may not truly grasp the full picture when it comes to SWIFT!Why do people keep linking various cryptocurrencies to SWIFT?Here’s the key: the logic centers on three distinct roles:🔥 XRP = LiquidityFacilitates the flow of funds, enabling the rapid transfer of… pic.twitter.com/hh4a1zhj0w

Algorand’s better matched with SWIFT POC aspirations for now. XRP currently uses classical elliptic-curve signatures, known as secp256k1 / Ed25519. No post-quantum signatures are live on the Ledger’s mainnet. The high-standard approach is going to be tested in 2027, while SWIFT is already piloting a roster of Ripple-linked banks.

Santander, Standard Chartered, HSBC & Deutsche Bank are the highlights of a double-digit list, but that doesn’t necessarily mean XRP coin is used as collateral or settlement. The chain’s On-Demand Liquidity (ODL) provides an additional liquidity layer via XRP, but it’s optional.

The bigger question is whether XRP can become a standard settlement layer on cross-border corridors.

The more interesting detail is how quickly the position has grown.

Lookonchain’s transaction monitoring history shows that by November 19, the wallet had withdrawn around 1.9 trillion PEPE from Binance. That figure climbed to 2.878 trillion by November 23 and exceeded 3.3 trillion the following day.

On Wednesday, Lookonchain reported that the address had accumulated 4.16 trillion tokens. By Thursday, its reported holdings had reached 5.15 trillion.

Another wallet, beginning with 0x6246, accumulated 868.16 billion PEPE valued at approximately $2.88 million, bringing the combined reported value to more than $21 million.

Large withdrawals are nothing new for the memecoin. NewsBTC previously covered a separate PEPE whale moving $14.7 million out of Binance. What makes the latest activity particularly interesting is the repeated accumulation within such a short period.

Before treating these transactions as a bullish signal, it’s worth looking at what other large holders have been doing.

Data from blockchain analytics platform Deep Blue Alpha showed that withdrawals accounted for approximately 36% of tracked PEPE whale transfers between wallets and exchanges over the preceding seven days, according to its November 26 update.

In other words, exchange deposits outweighed withdrawals within that particular group of wallets.

That doesn’t invalidate Lookonchain’s findings. It does, however, complicate the idea that large investors are collectively preparing for a PEPE recovery.

One group of holders may be increasing its exposure while others are looking to reduce theirs. The distinction matters, especially in a market where a handful of transactions can attract more attention than the activity of dozens of other wallets.

Exchange deposits aren’t necessarily sales, just as withdrawals don’t establish that a fresh purchase has taken place. Centralized exchange trading records remain largely invisible to outside observers.

For an investor holding 5.15 trillion PEPE, even a movement of $0.000001 in the token’s price would change the value of the position by $5.15 million.

That illustrates both the attraction and the risk of holding such a large quantity of a speculative asset.

Building an $18 million position is one thing. Exiting it at the quoted market price is another. The amount an investor can actually realize depends on available liquidity, execution and the market’s ability to absorb the tokens.

Concentrated holdings can therefore work in both directions. If tokens remain outside exchanges, they may reduce the supply immediately available for trading. If the same tokens return to exchanges, traders may suddenly find themselves watching for potential selling pressure.

The next development worth following is whether these wallets continue accumulating or begin transferring tokens back to trading platforms.

For now, two addresses hold an unusually large amount of PEPE. Whether the rest of the market shares their apparent appetite for the memecoin is a different question.

#5089. Bitcoin’s $60,000 recovery masks a growing threat that could push its price as low as $29,000

Galaxy Research says Bitcoin has exceeded historical bear market timelines while failing to meet 11 of its 13 historical bottom indicators.

Bitcoin recovered above $60,000 after slipping below that mark on Nov. 25, in a volatile week in which Bitcoin fell to around $55,000, its lowest level since September 2024.

BTC rebounded to $63,000 on Monday, but subsequently surrendered much of those gains.

According to Talos, Bitcoin lost 7.9% over the week, compared with declines of 2.9% for the S&P 500, 4.5% for the Nasdaq 100 and 7.8% for gold. Over 30 days, Bitcoin has fallen 25.3%, approximately 2.6 times the Nasdaq 100's decline.

Bitcoin's correlation with traditional risk assets has also strengthened. Its 30-day correlations with the S&P 500, Nasdaq 100 and Nvidia climbed to 0.78, 0.77 and 0.68, respectively, roughly 1.4 to twice their one-year medians.

Galaxy Research noted that Bitcoin's recent struggles are particularly unusual given its September recovery above the 50-week moving average, which has historically helped identify the end of bear markets.

Bitcoin has since fallen below both its 50-week and 200-week moving averages, breaking a recovery pattern that had held since 2011.

Bitcoin reclaimed its 50-week moving average in September after spending 44 consecutive weeks below it. It held above the indicator for seven weeks, reaching a daily close of $86,521 on Oct. 4, nearly 48% above its June low.

Galaxy found that none of the seven previous recoveries that sustained the moving average for at least seven weeks later produced a new bear-market low, even intraday.

September's recovery differed from earlier instances in one significant respect. Previous recoveries after prolonged periods below the moving average followed declines of 76.7% to 92.7%, whereas September's followed a comparatively shallow 53% drawdown on a closing basis.

Bitcoin's subsequent decline to $55,100 on Nov. 21 prompted Galaxy to withdraw its October assessment that the bear market ended in June.

The breakdown shifts attention to Bitcoin's June 30 closing low of $58,525.

Galaxy identified seven completed instances in which Bitcoin closed below a bear market low that had held for at least 60 days and from which the cryptocurrency had rebounded at least 20%.

All seven resulted in further declines of at least 17.1%, with a median loss of 51.8%. Applied to Bitcoin's June closing low, those historical outcomes would put the cryptocurrency at approximately $48,500 and $28,200, respectively.

However, another closing low would push Bitcoin beyond the historical duration of its bear markets.

As of Nov. 22, 412 days had elapsed since Bitcoin reached its record closing price of $124,824 in October 2025. Its four previous bear markets took between 163 and 406 days to bottom.

The current downturn has also exceeded historical halving-to-bottom timelines. The three previous cycle lows occurred between 777 and 912 days after their respective halvings, compared with the 946 days since Bitcoin's April 2024 halving.

While those timelines suggest Bitcoin is overdue for a recovery, its valuation and investor behavior point toward an unfinished bear market.

Please enable JavaScript to verify and send this form.

Bitcoin's previous four bear markets recorded peak-to-trough closing-price declines of approximately 93%, 85%, 84% and 77%, respectively.

Successive downturns have become shallower, but the largest reduction between previous cycles was eight percentage points. A bottom at the June closing low would represent a 24% reduction.

The divergence extends to Bitcoin's realized price, which estimates the aggregate cost basis of its circulating supply.

During previous bear markets, Bitcoin spent between 140 and 304 days below its realized price. It has yet to register a single daily close below that level, which stood at $53,205 on Nov. 22.

Meanwhile, the proportion of Bitcoin's supply held at a loss reached 57% on Nov. 20, within the 55% to 61% range recorded at previous cycle bottoms.

Despite that financial distress, Bitcoin's 30-day realized losses peaked at just 3.6% of its realized capitalization in February, compared with peaks of 7.3% to 16.7% during previous bear markets.

Investor sentiment has deteriorated more sharply. Galaxy's proprietary Bitcoin Fear & Greed Index fell to 5.2 on Nov. 21, its lowest reading since June 2022 and among the lowest 0.5% of historical readings.

Yet the index has spent just six days at or below 10 during the current downturn, compared with between 12 and 57 days during previous bear markets, including the month following their bottoms.

Derivatives traders have also maintained relatively resilient positioning. Bitcoin perpetual futures funding averaged a positive annualized rate of 4.3% over the seven days through Nov. 22, compared with negative 24.5% shortly after the November 2022 bottom.

As of Nov. 22, Bitcoin satisfied just two of the 13 historical bottom indicators Galaxy tracks.

The conflict between BTC's historical cycle duration and the depth of its losses leaves Galaxy examining two potential scenarios.

If cycle timelines prevail, several valuation measures point to potential support between $48,400 and $53,200. These include Bitcoin's realized price, its long-term holder cost basis, and the smallest historical decline following the breakdown of an established bear market low.

A bottom within that range would still represent Bitcoin's shallowest bear market on record.

However, a return to the valuation extremes that characterized previous downturns could push Bitcoin toward levels between $29,100 and $46,100.

Galaxy is also monitoring US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded products, which have shed 71,339 BTC worth $4.95 billion since October. Their holdings have declined to approximately 1.24 million BTC, just 1.5% above their July trough.

A break below that 1.22 million BTC trough, alongside a weekly close below Bitcoin's realized price, would strengthen the case for a deeper downturn.

Conversely, reclaiming the 200-week moving average at $68,159 and subsequently the 50-week average at $74,401 would move Galaxy back toward its October recovery thesis.

#5087. Binance Announces Dividends for Nvidia and Other Stocks

Binance will pay dividends to holders of stock tokens representing five companies: Nvidia, PayPal, Qualcomm, Western Digital, and Wendy’s.

The exchange will use the dividends paid by these companies to buy more stock tokens, allowing users to increase their holdings of the same stocks through the bStocks program.

The most important date for Nvidia token holders is Dec. 2. That's when Binance will take a snapshot of NVDAB balances at 01:00 UTC.

The snapshot for Wendy’s is scheduled for Dec. 1, followed by Nvidia on Dec. 2 and Qualcomm on Dec. 3.

Snapshots for PayPal and Western Digital are both scheduled for Dec. 4.

All snapshots will take place at 01:00 UTC.

In its Nov. 27 announcement, Binance provided the dates that will determine eligibility for dividends.

Binance plans to use Nvidia's cash dividends to purchase additional Nvidia shares, including fractional shares, after deducting applicable withholding taxes, fees, and other charges.

The proceeds will then be distributed among users who hold NVDAB on Binance and qualify for the dividend payment.

The same process will apply to the other four stocks.

If you hold eligible tokens in other products on the platform, such as savings or margin accounts, Binance will still credit the dividends to your spot account.

If you hold bStocks on-chain, the dividend payments will be made by adjusting the token's multiplier.

The tokens themselves are issued by Binance affiliate BTECH Holdings Limited, which owns the underlying securities.

So if you hold NVDAB, you have an interest in the Nvidia shares held by BTECH.

If you need to transfer tokens to Binance before the snapshot, you must do so at least two hours in advance.

Deposits and withdrawals of Nvidia tokens will be suspended at 23:00 UTC on Dec. 1.

The balance snapshot will take place at 01:00 UTC on Dec. 2.

Binance will also suspend one-to-one conversions between Nvidia shares and NVDAB tokens during this period.

The same two-hour suspension rule will apply to the other four stock tokens.

However, spot trading against USDT will continue, including trading in the NVDAB/USDT pair.

Binance said it would resume deposits, withdrawals and stock-to-token conversions after the dividend allocations are completed.

The exchange will not issue a separate announcement when these services resume.
